findings.title: Invalid ERB `end if` will prevent the template from rendering
findings.body: The first conditional is closed with `<%- end if %>`, which compiles to invalid Ruby (`end if` is not legal). Rendering the `best` embed view will raise a syntax error. It should be a plain `<% end %>`.

findings.title: Client-controlled Referer is interpolated into JavaScript without JavaScript escaping
findings.body: The embed layout outputs `parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>')`. The Referer header is controlled by the embedding page and is not escaped for JavaScript. A crafted referer can break the script context or potentially inject JavaScript into the Discourse origin, and it also controls the postMessage target origin. Use `escape_javascript`/`to_json` and validate the target origin explicitly.

findings.title: URL scheme validation uses line-start anchor instead of string-start anchor
findings.body: `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` uses `^`, which in Ruby matches the beginning of any line. A multiline string containing a non-http scheme followed by a newline and an http URL can pass this check. Use `\A` (and preferably validate the whole URL) to enforce the scheme.

findings.title: Imported URL is interpolated into raw HTML footer without escaping
findings.body: `TopicEmbed.import` appends `"#{url}"` to imported content. The URL is only loosely checked and is not HTML-escaped. Since imported posts use the `raw_html` cook method and are rendered with `raw`, a malicious URL containing quotes, tags, or script can produce stored XSS.

findings.title: `import` assumes `contents` is a non-nil mutable string
findings.body: `TopicEmbed.import` immediately mutates its `contents` argument with `contents << ...`. If a caller passes nil (possible from feed/readability extraction) or a frozen string, the import raises instead of failing cleanly. Validate or normalize the content before appending.

findings.title: `raw_html` cook method bypasses sanitization and is rendered raw
findings.body: The new `cook` path returns `raw` unchanged when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. Imported external HTML is untrusted, and the embed view renders `post.cooked` with `raw`. Without sanitization this enables stored XSS from feeds or retrieved embed pages.

findings.title: `import_remote` opens the URL before validating scheme or safely restricting it
findings.body: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url).read` before `TopicEmbed.import` applies its http/https check, and `TopicRetriever` only compares the URI host to `embeddable_host`. A URL with a matching host but non-HTTP scheme can reach `open`, allowing unintended fetches or local file access if an open-uri handler supports it. Validate scheme and URL format before opening.

findings.title: postMessage origin check uses substring matching
findings.body: The listener accepts messages when `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) !== -1`. This is not an exact origin comparison; an origin that is a prefix or substring of `discourseUrl` can pass. Compare `e.origin` against the parsed origin of `discourseUrl` exactly.

findings.title: Feed items without content crash the poller
findings.body: `i.content.scrub` assumes every feed item has a content field. RSS/ATOM items may have only description/summary or nil content, causing `NoMethodError`. With `retry: false`, the scheduled job stops. Handle nil content and fall back to other item fields.

findings.title: Post side effects are enqueued before the outer embed transaction commits
findings.body: Inside `Topic.transaction`, `PostCreator#create` runs and enqueues jobs/publishes messages after its own inner transaction but before the surrounding `TopicEmbed` transaction commits. If `TopicEmbed.create!` later fails and the outer transaction rolls back, asynchronous work remains queued for records that were not persisted.

findings.title: Check-then-create embed can raise unique-index errors under concurrency
findings.body: `import` checks for an existing `TopicEmbed` and then creates one, while the database has a unique index on `embed_url`. Concurrent first imports of the same URL can both pass the check; one will raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`. Rescue the unique violation and reload/use the existing record.

findings.title: Redis throttle key is set and expired non-atomically
findings.body: `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)` is not atomic. If the process crashes between the two calls, the key can remain without TTL and permanently throttle retrieval for that embed URL. Use an atomic SET with NX and expiration.

findings.title: Embed content SHA is updated even if the revision fails
findings.body: After `PostRevisor#revise!`, `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` runs unconditionally. If the post cannot be revised or saved, the stored SHA no longer matches the post content, causing future content changes to be skipped. Check the revision result before updating the SHA.

findings.title: `absolutize_urls` can raise on borderline URLs
findings.body: `URI(url)` is called without rescuing `URI::InvalidURIError`. The preceding URL check only requires an http(s) prefix, so strings with spaces or other invalid characters can reach this method and crash import/retrieval jobs. Validate or rescue invalid URLs and skip them.

findings.title: `force: true` will drop an existing topic_embeds table
findings.body: The migration creates `topic_embeds` with `force: true`, which drops the table first. If the table already exists from a prior installation or branch, existing embed mappings are destroyed. Avoid `force: true` in migrations that may run against existing data.

findings.title: Adding `force: true` to the top_topics migration can drop data
findings.body: Changing `create_table :top_topics` to use `force: true` makes the migration drop and recreate the table if rerun. This can silently delete existing `top_topics` data. Migrations should not destructively recreate tables that may already contain production data.

findings.title: Script throws if `discourse-comments` element is absent
findings.body: `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` may return null on pages that include `embed.js` but do not have the expected container. The subsequent `comments.appendChild(iframe)` throws and prevents the embed from loading. Guard against the missing element.
